utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: At this time, I'll turn it over to Councilmember Lee.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I just want to second Chair Hankerson's request to try to look into

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: you know, joining applications and, you know, making it more efficient.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And I would love to do that in other agencies as well.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Not just parks, but...

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Yeah, so I just want to second that one.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And also, I have the great fortune to have amazing parks in my district.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I have Elipon, Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: We're actually doing a health fair in Cunningham Park this Sunday, which should be exciting.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: But I asked my staff in particular if they had any, knowing the topic, like as members of our office, you know, when you guys are applying for these permits, what are some pain points potentially or things that even as elected offices that you sort of run into with challenges?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so, but before I ask that question, just really, can you go back to, and I know that Chair Hankerson asked this, but how many folks are in the events permitting in Queens again?

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: One moment, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Okay, sorry.

chapters.summary: Lee asks when and why the $721 wanger wagon fee was added. Cerrone explains the wanger wagon is a mobile stage requiring a tow truck, CDL driver, and additional staff, taking park supervisors away from cleanup and maintenance duties.
chapters.title: Linda Lee asks about $721 wanger wagon fee

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: In Queens, it's six.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Six, okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then for the larger events that need to go to the citywide special events team, how many folks are there?

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Eight, okay.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So these are going to be oddly specific questions, sorry, because I didn't even know what a wanger wagon was.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then so I know that there's now a fee of the $721 that we would be charged that we would have to use from our office budgets if we wanted to have a wanger wagon at one of our events.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so just wondering when that charge was added, why, if you could go a little bit into that.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And I have to admit, before I started doing this work, I did not know what a wanger wagon was either.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: So, you know, you're not alone in that.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: The policy, I believe, was updated in the prior fiscal year.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: But if it's okay, I'd kind of like to walk you through what the kind of rationale was.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: When you have a wanger wagon, which for your other colleagues, it's a mobile stage.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And they are sizable.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: I don't recall off the top of my head the exact dimensions, but it's kind of like you're driving a trailer truck.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: So you need a vehicle that's called a totter to bring the wanger wagon from one location to another.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And to drive that, you need a special driver's license.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: The CDL, commercial driver's license.

utterances.speaker: Ty Hankerson
utterances.text: License, yeah.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And so there's only a select number of people in each borough who have that.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And they tend to be, I think, the park supervisors.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And generally speaking, on any given day, we have about one park supervisor in a district.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And those are the people that drive our packers and our heavy-duty vehicles.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: So what we realized is we were kind of looking at our park ratings and our ability to clean our parks is that we were taking these people.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Out of the park effectively for an entire day.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Because when you're getting a wanger wagon, you have to get the

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: a totter first, then you have to drive it over to the wagon because they tend to be in separate places because the totters are used for other activities as well.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Then you have to drive it to the event location.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And not only that, you have to take an additional staff person with you because when you're driving that around,

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: You know, it's not unusual for the location where the Wenger wagon would be kind of unfolded to be in an interior of a park.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And that means we need someone else out there making sure that no one is injured.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: There's no kids, you know, driving by on scooters or anything.

chapters.summary: Lee asks why bouncy houses trigger the 500-person threshold. Cerrone says Parks lowered the threshold to 200 and cites injuries from tipped bouncy houses as a reason for more regulation.
chapters.title: Linda Lee asks about bouncy house threshold and safety

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And so you're effectively taking two staff people.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: For the entire day.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And it is just, you know, it has become something that is a big time commitment.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And we take those people out of the day.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: So they're not driving our heavy duty equipment.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: They're not driving our packers.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: They're not able to pick up the trash or respond to any other needs within a park district.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: So what we've had to do is,

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: We have to call people in on overtime in order to provide those services.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: We still want to provide them, and we do that with you and your colleagues in the city council and with other agencies.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: But it had just reached a point where operationally it became challenging.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: No, that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that.

utterances.text: And then also for...

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: events that our offices host, like, for example, the one we're doing on Sunday with our health fair or family fun days, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I know that, you know, if we have bouncy houses or other things like that, it requires that 500 person threshold.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: But can you go a little bit more into.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Why that 500 person threshold is needed for things like bouncy houses and also what other things sort of trigger that 500 person threshold.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Thank you for bringing that up, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: That is something I wanted to mention.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And, Ann, or Gabby, please correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: I believe that we've lowered that number, and it is no longer 500.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: I believe that it is, you know, meaning it's 200.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And so it's much more accessible for smaller events.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And we had heard from you and from your colleagues that that was a little bit of a challenge, and we took another look at it, and we've changed it.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: I can tell you, you know, I'm a very, you know, proud parent.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And, you know, when my kids see a bouncy house, it's like there's like this gravitational pull, you know.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Yeah, there is.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: You can't tell them no.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And so, like, we, but we have also, what we found is, like, when we permitted these teams, it really depends on who the contractor is.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: And, like, we've had times when.

utterances.text: Like these things have tipped over.

utterances.text: And like there's been, you know, kids have gotten hurt and broken bones.

utterances.text: And so we're trying to kind of manage that.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone
utterances.text: But with council members, you know, it is something that is continuing on.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone

utterances.text: That is not something that we're utilizing.

utterances.text: And we've lowered the capacity to 200.

utterances.text: So I hope that that's helpful.

utterances.text: But, you know, I think our team, our public programs team that does bouncing houses internally, you know, we're starting to see the instances tick up where, you know, not certainly through a council member's office, but just when people were having them.

utterances.text: There were accidents that seemed preventable, and we wanted to try and have a little bit more kind of regulation around it.

utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.text: We could certainly do that looking back.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone

utterances.text: What is DPR's review process after an event is concluded to determine whether it was successful or not?

utterances.text: We want people to have fun.

utterances.speaker: David Cerrone

summary: Committee on Parks and Recreation held an oversight hearing on NYC Parks' special events permitting process, with testimony from Deputy Commissioner David Cerrone and Anne McTiernan.
Council members questioned Parks about late approvals, denial data, staffing, transparency, insurance, unpermitted events, security, and post-event restoration; Parks committed to several follow-ups.

The committee also considered Intro 927 to rename Shorefront Parkway in Queens as Edgemere Avenue and heard public testimony from Christopher Leon Johnson and City Parks Foundation's Heather Lubov before adjourning.
